newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 8.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Nov 8:

WASHINGTON - President Clinton said he will consider Republicans for top jobs in his second administration, a bipartisan approach that he plans to amplify with a call for early talks with Republican congressional leaders on the budget and campaign finance reform.
WASHINGTON - The Democratic National Committee returned its second large contribution in two days, bringing to about $750,000 the amount the party has been forced to give back.

WASHINGTON - Three hours before the scheduled execution, Virginia Governor George Allen commuted the death sentence of a convicted murderer to life without parole after an intense campaign for clemency that included appeals from four jurors and the murder victim's mother.

WASHINGTON - The U.S. hard liquor industry said it would break its decade-old voluntary ban on television and radio advertising of spirits, a decision greeted with dismay by regulators and anti-alcohol groups.
WASHINGTON - The U.S. Army has charged three military trainers in an alleged rape and sexual harassment case involving at least 17 female soldiers at a Maryland base.

PARIS - As the human toll in eastern Zaire threatened to assume what one relief worker termed "apocalypse" proportions, Western and African governments continued to meet, talk and argue about the most effective way to respond to the crisis.
